reuse.why: The change reuses getApproxNumberThreshold and shares the new resolver across four consumers, but introduces a parallel abstraction beside the existing getScheduledAmount.

duplication.why: The migrated consumers share their decision, but the new helper duplicates getScheduledAmount's missing-value and numeric dispatch while leaving other amount resolvers separate.

placement.why: Schedule amount policy belongs in shared/schedules.ts, with API serialization delegating to it and tolerance calculation remaining in shared/rules.ts.

scope.why: All edits concern expected schedule amounts, their API representation, or directly related tests.

maintainability.why: The new helper is compact, but competing schedule amount definitions, an unrestricted string operator, and outdated policy comments make future changes harder to maintain consistently.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts adds getExpectedScheduleAmount alongside getScheduledAmount instead of evolving the existing schedule amount abstraction.

disguised_duplication.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount reshapes the existing getScheduledAmount resolver under a new name, retaining its missing-value and numeric dispatch while supplying a separate range policy.

abstraction_drift.where: The new resolver adds an optional op parameter and an isapprox branch; getScheduledAmount, forecast/forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule, and budget/schedule-template.ts createScheduleList retain independent amount decisions outside it.
